```{r message=FALSE}
library(TwoSampleMR)
```

```{r, eval=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
# Get data for the vignette (`ao` is cut down to the studies the vignette names)
ao <- available_outcomes()
bmi_exp_dat <- extract_instruments(outcomes = "ukb-b-19953")
chd_out_dat1 <- extract_outcome_data(
  snps = bmi_exp_dat$SNP,
  outcomes = "ebi-a-GCST003116"
)
chd_out_dat2 <- extract_outcome_data(
  snps = bmi_exp_dat$SNP,
  outcomes = c("ukb-b-19953", "ebi-a-GCST003116")
)
save(ao, bmi_exp_dat, chd_out_dat1, chd_out_dat2, file = file.path("inst", "extdata", "vig_outcome.RData"), compress = "xz")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, warning=FALSE}
load(system.file("extdata", "vig_outcome.RData", package = "TwoSampleMR"))
```

Once instruments for the exposure trait have been specified, those variants need to be extracted from the outcome trait.

## Available studies in the OpenGWAS database

The OpenGWAS database contains complete GWAS summary statistics from a large number of studies. You can browse them here:

https://opengwas.io

TwoSampleMR reads it through the [opengwasr](https://github.com/opengwas/opengwasr) package, which needs an OpenGWAS token (see `vignette("opengwasr", package = "opengwasr")`). To obtain details about the available GWASs programmatically do the following:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
ao <- available_outcomes()
```

(Here `ao` is cut down to a few studies, so that this vignette builds without the network.)

```{r}
head(ao[, c("id", "analysis_label", "assigned_ancestry", "sample_size")])
```

The `available_outcomes()` function returns a table of all the available studies (Analyses) in the database. Each study has a unique ID of the form `<store_id>:<analysis_id>`, and `analysis_label` is its trait. The old IDs, such as `ukb-b-19953`, are accepted wherever they name one study.

## Extracting particular SNPs from particular studies

If we want to perform MR of BMI against coronary artery disease, we need to identify the SNPs that influence the BMI, and then extract those SNPs from a GWAS on coronary artery disease.

Let's get the instruments for BMI from the UK Biobank study as an example:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
bmi_exp_dat <- extract_instruments(outcomes = "ukb-b-19953")
```

```{r}
head(bmi_exp_dat[, 1:12])
```

We now need to find a suitable GWAS for coronary artery disease. We can search the available studies:

```{r}
ao[grepl("coronary", ao$analysis_label, ignore.case = TRUE), c("id", "analysis_label", "sample_size", "n_cases")]
```

The CARDIoGRAMplusC4D 2015 GWAS is `ebi-a-GCST003116` (its full ID is `OGS-00011:GCST003116`). We can extract the BMI SNPs from this GWAS as follows:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
chd_out_dat1 <- extract_outcome_data(
  snps = bmi_exp_dat$SNP,
  outcomes = "ebi-a-GCST003116"
)
```

The `extract_outcome_data()` function is flexible. The `snps` argument only requires an array of rsIDs (or ALIDs, `chromosome:position:effect allele:other allele` on GRCh38), and the `outcomes` argument can be a vector of outcomes, e.g.
```{r eval=FALSE}
chd_out_dat2 <- extract_outcome_data(
  snps = bmi_exp_dat$SNP,
  outcomes = c("ukb-b-19953", "ebi-a-GCST003116")
)
```

will extract the SNPs from each of the outcomes `ukb-b-19953` and `ebi-a-GCST003116`. A study that does not exist is an error.

## Imputed Associations, not LD proxies

Earlier versions of TwoSampleMR searched for an LD proxy (a SNP in LD with the requested SNP) whenever a requested SNP was not in the outcome GWAS. That no longer happens. The OpenGWAS data are now Reference-Completed: for most variants that a study did not report, OpenGWAS holds an *Imputed Association*, estimated from the study's reported variants. `extract_outcome_data()` returns it as the requested variant itself, not as a proxy, and `association_status.outcome` says whether each Association is `"observed"` or `"imputed"`.

```{r}
table(chd_out_dat1$association_status.outcome)
```

`harmonise_data()` reports how many of the outcome Associations used for MR were Imputed, and `mr()` gives their number in `nsnp_imputed`. The arguments that controlled proxies (`proxies`, `rsq`, `palindromes`, `maf_threshold`, `align_alleles` and `proxy_splitsize`) are still accepted, but print a message and change nothing.

## Using local GWAS summary data

If you have GWAS summary data that is not present in the OpenGWAS database, this can still be used to perform analysis.

Supposing there is a GWAS summary file called "gwas_summary.csv" with e.g. 2 million rows and it looks like this:

```
rsid,effect,SE,a1,a2,a1_freq,p-value,Units,Gene,n
rs10767664,0.19,0.030612245,A,T,0.78,5.00E-26,kg/m2,BDNF,225238
rs13078807,0.1,0.020408163,G,A,0.2,4.00E-11,kg/m2,CADM2,221431
rs1514175,0.07,0.020408163,A,G,0.43,8.00E-14,kg/m2,TNNI3K,207641
rs1558902,0.39,0.020408163,A,T,0.42,5.00E-120,kg/m2,FTO,222476
...
...
```

To extract the exposure SNPs from this data, we would use the following command:

```{r eval=FALSE}
outcome_dat <- read_outcome_data(
  snps = bmi_exp_dat$SNP,
  filename = "gwas_summary.csv",
  sep = ",",
  snp_col = "rsid",
  beta_col = "effect",
  se_col = "SE",
  effect_allele_col = "a1",
  other_allele_col = "a2",
  eaf_col = "a1_freq",
  pval_col = "p-value",
  units_col = "Units",
  gene_col = "Gene",
  samplesize_col = "n"
)
```

This returns an outcome data frame with only the SNPs that were requested (if those SNPs were present in the "gwas_summary.csv" file).

## Outcome data format

The `extract_outcome_data` function returns a table of SNP effects for the requested SNPs on the requested outcomes. The format of the data is similar to the exposure data format, except the main columns are as follows:

- `SNP`
- `beta.outcome`
- `se.outcome`
- `samplesize.outcome`
- `ncase.outcome`
- `ncontrol.outcome`
- `pval.outcome`
- `eaf.outcome`
- `effect_allele.outcome`
- `other_allele.outcome`
- `outcome`
- `id.outcome`
- `originalname.outcome`
- `effect_scale.outcome` - `"sd"` (per SD of the trait) or `"log_or"` (log odds ratio)
- `association_status.outcome` - `"observed"` or `"imputed"`
- `mr_keep.outcome`
- `data_source.outcome`

## More advanced use of local data

We have developed a summary data format called "GWAS VCF", which is designed to store GWAS results in a strict and performant way. It is possible to use this format with the TwoSampleMR package. For more details, see this package that explains the format and how to query it in R:

https://github.com/mrcieu/gwasvcf

and this package for how to connect the data to other packages including TwoSampleMR

https://github.com/MRCIEU/gwasglue
